root_idea.summary: The root develops along two principal axes: making an incision, breach, or damaging penetration, and drawing or ladling something out.
root_idea.development: The first axis includes striking to produce fire, corrosion, piercing, and figurative impugning; the second includes ladling from a vessel or well and the vessel or residue associated with that action. These root-level developments do not make every branch a meaning of the Quranic form.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The sole Quran-attested group is presented under the normalized verbal-noun citation form قَدْحٌ.

senses.definition: Striking or producing fire, especially the striking that elicits sparks.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun used in the Quranic construction قَدْحًا; in the supplied occurrence it denotes fire-producing striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To canker or corrode trees, wood, or teeth.
To impair or attack someone's honor, reputation, genealogy, or standing; to blame, censure, or reproach; also, to impugn a witness's rectitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with expressions such as قَدَحَ فِي عِرْضِهِ, قَدَحَ فِي نَسَبِهِ, and قَدَحَ فِي عَدَالَتِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a hole in the end of an arrow-shaft for insertion of the tang of its iron head.
To break the sealed clay on the mouth of a jar.
To couch an eye by extracting its corrupt fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An operative medical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an impression in the bosom or mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ladle broth or another liquid out with a ladle, including from the bottom of a pot or well.
For an eye to sink or become depressed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The eye is described as becoming like a قَدَح.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a horse lean, lank, or slender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The comparison is with the slenderness of an arrow-shaft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual reviling or contending in altercation, dispute, or litigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes reciprocal foul or unseemly speech; the corresponding verb denotes contending or disputing with someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with one another in altercation or dispute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or make use of another person's instrumentality or means.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use of making fire with another's fire-making implement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consider and examine an affair in order to elicit its likely issue or result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask or demand the use of another person's instrumentality or means.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative use based on asking another's fire-making implement to produce fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A canker or corrosion in trees or teeth; also rottenness, decay, corruption, or unsoundness, and a crack or fissure in wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same noun is also used for blackness appearing in the teeth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow-shaft or pared rod before it is furnished with feathers and a head, or after it has been straightened and prepared for them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word especially includes an arrow used in the game of maysir; its plural is قِدَاحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A drinking-cup or bowl, large enough in one usage to satisfy the thirst of two men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A well-known vessel; plural أَقْدَاحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A measure of capacity used in Egypt, containing two hundred and thirty-two dirhams.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional metrological use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act of striking or producing fire.
An elicitation, by examination, of the real state or nature of a case or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act of ladling broth or another liquid out.
A ladleful of broth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form is used in requests for a portion of broth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of striking or producing fire with a fire-making implement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also be extended to the faculty of producing light or darkness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Consideration and examination of an affair to elicit its possible issue or result.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A common fly, described as though producing fire by rubbing its forelegs together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative or descriptive naming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well whose water is drawn by hand in successive ladings.
The pieces of wood belonging to a camel saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective word without a singular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broth, especially what remains at the bottom of a cooking-pot and is ladled out with difficulty.
The craft of making vessels called أَقْدَاح.
An epithet for a fire-making stick or implement that produces much fire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a زَنْد.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of vessels called أَقْدَاح.
The blossoms of plants before they open, or the fresh, juicy tips, leaves, suckers, or offsets of plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A regional or dialectal botanical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone from which fire is struck.
One who ladles out; in a conventional description, water whose scant quantity keeps its ladler from sleeping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The latter sense is preserved as an idiomatic description of very little water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A canker-worm that corrodes trees and teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Collective plural قَوَادِحُ is also attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A couching needle used in an eye operation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical instrument.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron implement with which fire is struck.
A ladle.
Lean, lank, or slender, especially of horses made slender like arrow-shafts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to horses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a sunken or depressed eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to an eye and, by extension, to horses whose eyes are sunken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing trees with soft, weak branches that flare with fire when moved by the wind but yield no useful fire when deliberately used for that purpose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A literal descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A figurative expression for someone lacking a sound claim to honor, respect, or good parentage, genealogy, or pedigree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative idiom based on the preceding tree description.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Inchoative fire-production variant covered by the fire-striking sense.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the inflected form قَدْحًا; it is normalized here to the verbal-noun citation form قَدْحٌ, despite the QAC generic noun tag.
